gaps.text: Still the 36-line stub: 8 grey boxes, tan plane, NO ceiling at all. Biggest gap in the project.

Content gap, not a rendering gap. (1) Product facings are flat colour fields with grey bars instead of real printed type — ~60% of the tell. (2) ~8 box meshes recoloured, 5-8 identical copies per shelf; real shelves carry 6-15 SKUs of mixed height/width and something on nearly every shelf is a bottle/jar/pouch/bag. (3) Zero 'shopped' disorder — every face perfectly flush, unrotated, evenly spaced, no sold-out voids.

Contact shadows / AO is now the single biggest tell — products have no darkening where they meet the deck, shelf cavities do not fall off to near-black, so shelves read as decals floating on a plane. Then: no per-instance variation WITHIN a facing block (20 identical chip bags, same lean, zero gaps); shelves 100% full when real stores run 10-20% gaps; everything the same matte diffuse with zero specular events.

The two surfaces filling the largest solid angle of the frame — ceiling and floor — are still flat-shaded planes with a texture on them. (1) The floor returns ZERO specular under a lit ceiling; every real photo shows the ceiling light rows mirrored as long vertical smears. 'Until light physically bounces off the floor, nothing further up the list will matter.' (2) Ceiling troffers are emissive quads coplanar with the tile, not recessed housings with tube shapes and a shadow line. (3) BINARY TELLS: an unlit pink placeholder cube on a grey stick, untextured grey cart proxies, a blank grey plane where a sign texture failed. Any one ends the test alone.

gaps.text: Measured 58% catch rate with NO powerup. Bar is near 0% — powerups are currently pointless and the chase has no tension.

bench() measures a starting geometry the game never produces. bench() spawns the cop 4.32m BEHIND the thief (gapMul 0.96 x suspicionRadius, already at 0.7x copRun). game.js enterFloor(i) spawns him at (aisleX(i), 0, -AISLE_LEN/2+3) — the MOUTH of the thief's aisle, between the thief and the only exit. Measured from the real start with powerups deleted from the store: 100% catch, no powerup (80/80 controlled, 14/14 full end-to-end game loop), chase over in ~1.2s median. Root cause is geometry, not speed: a corked 4m aisle is impassable — the thief's own nav avoid radius (1.8m, agents.js navToExit bolt case) is WIDER than the aisle half-lane (AISLE_GAP/2 - BODY_R = 1.58m), so he can never route around a cop standing in it and walks straight into the 1.15m catchRadius. Give him a way through (second exit / back-of-store route / a juke or shove past a blocking body), THEN re-run bench() from enterFloor()'s spawn — that is the only number that describes the game.

A corked 4m aisle is impassable: the thief's nav avoid radius (1.80m) is WIDER than the aisle half-lane (AISLE_GAP/2 - BODY_R = 1.58m), so he can never route around a cop standing in it and walks into the 1.15m catch radius. He needs counterplay — a back-of-store route, a second exit, or a juke past a blocking body. Then re-bench from enterFloor's actual spawn.

61% of correctly-dispatched chases (368/600) end with the grab inside 1s of the bolt: postSpawn parks the cop at a fixed z=-10 while the thief is uniform over a 22m aisle, so half the dispatches land inside 10m, and the corked thief's default is to run AT the cop, turning any gap into a ~1s head-on. Catch median from dispatch is 1.13s - FASTER than round 2's 1.7s. The 68->73% headline came from adding an escape hatch (25% route out the back, 0/270 caught if you follow), not from making the catches harder.

61.3% of correct dispatches end with the grab inside 1 SECOND of the bolt (84.4% of all catches). Median time-to-catch went 1.7s -> 1.13s: the catches got FASTER. The 68->73% headline came entirely from adding an escape hatch (the back route), not from making the catch harder. Chase is bimodal and each branch is near-deterministic: 449/600 run AT the cop -> 97.1% caught in 0.85s; 151/600 go out the back -> 0 caught, 0 for 270 unboosted. Builder's own bench prints catchUnder1s 120/200 and the report never mentions it.

Desk phase is near-unwinnable: ~12s from concealment tell to exit, 14 roster rows, only 3 of 7 subjects visible per camera.

Front-end dispatch is presented in the same confident amber as a winnable aisle call, but it is almost always a losing move — cop spawns ~20m behind a subject who is 10m from the door. Should read as the long shot it is, or players learn to distrust the button instead of learning to act earlier.

game.note: Two-door HUD deliberately REFUSES to read s.doorPref - printing the hidden preference would hand back the exact variable the two-door fix exists to hide. Reads the margin instead: outside doorBias no preference can change his destination, so it locks to ROUTE COMMITTED; inside the band it says BOTH DOORS LIVE and breaks ties on which door is closing faster. Measured naive-vs-biased read: disagree 6.2%, all inside the band where the panel already declines to commit. Attributed the stand-down fix via a FIX.close switch rather than seed-matched before/after, because eval.js patches Math.random so any change in RNG draw count re-rolls the stream.

Root causes, none of which were the reported symptom: the 'failing diffuser map' was ceiling clutter (conduit, sprinkler branches, dangler strings) hung INSIDE the troffer well between lamp plane and door. The olive ceiling was a Lambert plane whose normal points down, so the HemisphereLight fed it ground colour at full strength across the largest surface in the scene. Far-floor blowout was the reflection's across-aisle blur growing uncapped. Both 'placeholders' were real geometry, not failed textures - three unrelated sage greens at three depths reading as one void. AO was never weak: the light rig had ~half its budget arriving from everywhere at once, so occlusion cards were fighting flat fill.

r4b: found the real cause of the 'black shards on the diffuser map' — not the lens texture, but conduit/data cable/sprinkler branches/dangler strings hung at CEIL_H-0.05..0.15, i.e. INSIDE the 105mm troffer recess added in r4a. Added a CLUTTER_Y clearance plane below the door plane + offRow() to keep along-aisle runs off the light rows. Ceiling plane Lambert->Basic: its normal points down so the HemisphereLight was feeding it the ground colour at full strength, rendering acoustic tile as olive-brown mud. Capped the floor reflection's across-aisle blur (was growing 0.0075/m unbounded, so grazing rays washed the far half of every aisle floor into one featureless white sheet). Two-layer troffer bloom so distant runs merge into a continuous line. Killed the 'blank rectangle where a sign failed to load': it was three different greens at three depths (sage decor band + sage blade signs + green PRODUCE sign) — back wall band is now cream with pilasters and raised sign panels, blades are cream-on-dark. Lighting rebalanced from ~50% omnidirectional to directional-dominant. Edge density all 8 aisles: min 37.3 max 42.9 mean 41.0 (was min 32.2 max 39.0 mean 36.3).

Found a round-2 bug: every specular in the atlases was drawn white under multiply compositing - a no-op. Nothing in the store was ever glossy.

R3: cavity+deck AO (2-col multiply atlas, mouth AND deck-surface passes) as the headline fix; per-instance yaw/depth/scale/gap on every unit plus 2-3 deliberately wrong units per block (face-turned, crushed, leaning, shoved deep, missing); 12-18% vacancy with bare bays and orphan tag holders; Phong+per-texel gloss for cans/bottles/bags and a glint() that actually works (round 2 composited every sheen as white-under-multiply, a no-op, so nothing was glossy); gondola hardware — rails broken at every 4ft joint, punched-slot uprights, deck brackets, perforated back panels, wire dividers, clip strips, shelf wobblers; ceiling rebuilt — 4-state fixture atlas with dead/warm/dim tubes and jittered pitch, third light row, sprinkler GRID, conduit, speakers, ~90 danglers, 8x8 tile map with stains/grilles/heavy fissure grain; floor — VCT chip pattern at real density, non-repeating wear layer, per-fixture reflections, tinted gondola smear; back rows on every deck (was 1 row, 60% bare board); per-run merchandising profiles (tight/mixed/bulky/reset) for genuine aisle-to-aisle spread; full-depth perimeter runs with upper deck; powerups are now real merchandising (bakery dump table, iced barrel cooler, riser cards) with NO colliders. Root cause was NOT the avoid radius: nav.steer did greedy descent FIRST then filtered, so a corked aisle fouled every point, got=false, and it fell back to 'furthest visible point' — the far side of the cop. The thief sprinted INTO him. Fix prices the cop as a cost inside the Dijkstra flood, but ONLY downstream of the runner: without that filter a cop merely behind prices the ground the thief stands on and the stern chase leaks 1.3% -> 79%.

Confirms the coupling I flagged: observer catch fell 79.4% -> 59.7% once the chase stopped being unlosable, and points fell 1532 -> 912. The old figure was inflated by a chase that auto-caught. The skill separation survives the correction, which is the result that matters.

COUNTERPLAY: the cop is now a COST IN THE ESCAPE FLOOD, not a filter on an already-computed descent. Root cause of the cork: nav.steer's avoid ran AFTER a greedy gradient walk, so it could only pick a nearer point on the same line -- when every point was fouled it fell back to the far side of the cop and the thief sprinted into him. Threat now enters the Dijkstra cost (nav.field opt.avoid), gated to cells downstream of the runner so a pursuer behind him never bends his route. Plus: thief reacts when he SEES the aisle mouth blocked (8.6m, needs LOS + on his route line) instead of walking to 4.5m; tangential (not radial) cop avoidance while running; a committed shoulder-barge whose outcome depends on where the cop was standing when he committed -- hold the lane centre and you have him, drift off one side and he goes past the other for the price of a 0.45s stumble. Per-thief nerve so the route decision is not a pure function of position. FROM enterFloor's REAL SPAWN (cop in the aisle mouth), n=200: no powerup 68.0% (was 100/100 before), loses by 2.96m/9.7ft, escapes run 15.6s, 64/200 broke out the back. Powerup reachable 91.5%. Boost in hand 98.7%. Wrong aisle by 1/2/4: 44.7/34.7/23.3%. Front-end post 39.3%. Round-2's stern-chase bench preserved at 0.7%. Incidental free boosts 0.0%. bench() now defaults to the real spawn and mode:'none' actually removes the powerups.

Bench contradicted its own round-1 diagnosis: the 12s window was already 19-24s after the chase rewrite and the observer was already at 83.2%. Real defect was harassment firing on ANY shopper within 4.5m - in a 4m aisle every bystander you edge past files a complaint (0.75 demotions/shift). Fixed with contact-gated complaints + zone dispatch (DISPATCH greyed out for the last 20m of a thief's walk - 64.3% of the guesser's thieves hit that dead zone). Doubled burn-in fixed via cctv.floorBurnIn=false. Deleted the fabricated-escape watchdog: fired 0 times in 50 shift-minutes.

Benched the desk phase (src/game/eval.js: screen-limited perfect-observer bot vs random-guesser bot, 16x240s shifts each, n~220 thieves/policy). Diagnosis was wrong: the window was never the problem — agents' chase rewrite already widened conceal-to-door to a 19-24s median, and the R1 observer already caught 83.2%. The real defect was that the CORRECT player got fired anyway (0.75 demotions/shift) because harassment fired on any shopper inside a 4.5m radius, i.e. every bystander you edge past walking to the subject you correctly identified. Fix = complaints only file against the subject the reticle is actually on (a contact, not a shared aisle); plus dispatch now targets the subject's zone instead of demanding an aisle number, which removed a dead zone where the DISPATCH button greyed out for the last ~20m of the thief's walk to Door 1 (10.7-64.3% of thieves spent time in it); plus a scrolling roster and a PA price-check hold. BEFORE observer 83.2% catch / 0.75 demotions per shift / 693 pts per shift, random 35.0% / 3.13 / 93, idle 0% and one loss every 24.6s. AFTER observer 79.4% catch / 0 demotions / 1532 pts per shift, random 37.0% / 1.56 / 107. Reader now outscores guesser 14:1 and keeps the job; guesser is still fired every 1.5 shifts. Also: killed the doubled floor burn-in by setting cctv.floorBurnIn=false (HUD owns REC + clock), switched door ETA to agents.thiefCruise() and route distance per the chase note, and deleted the R1 wedge watchdog's fabricated-escape branch (fired 0 times in ~50 shift-minutes).

Contact shadows / AO is now the single biggest tell — products have no darkening where they meet the deck, shelf cavities do not fall off to near-black, so shelves read as decals floating on a plane. Then: no per-instance variation WITHIN a facing block (20 identical chip bags, same lean, zero gaps); shelves 100% full when real stores run 10-20% gaps; everything the same matte diffuse with zero specular events.

Real printed type on every facing: invented wordmarks in real faces, descriptors, nutrition panels, UPC blocks, 7-11 lines of legal type. 48 designs across cartons/pouches/cans/bottles via per-instance atlas cells. fillShelf is now a planogram with brand blocks and per-run irregular deck heights. Shopped disorder: depth wander, 20% rotated, sold-out voids, backwards/crushed items. Round 2: real printed type on every facing. New src/store/pack.js draws actual fillText glyphs (invented brands, product descriptors, flavour flashes, net-weight lines, Nutrition Facts panels, 7-11 lines of tiny legal type, UPC blocks) into 4 shared mask atlases; per-instance aCell UV offset picks the design, so 48 designs cost 1 draw call per batch instead of 1 geometry clone each. Mask channels now r=brand amount, g=print brightness (0.045+0.955g for real black type), b=4-band food palette keyed to the printed product name so canned peas render green and tomato paste red. Rewrote fillShelf as a planogram: brand blocks of 1-4 flavour varieties, kinds filtered to each deck's clear height, per-run irregular deck plans, aggressive stacking, per-item depth wander, 20% rotated 3-15deg, sold-out voids, backwards/crushed/lying-flat items, top-decks-forward vertical gradient. Cans/bottles now front-fold their label UV (was wrapping 3x and showing wordmark fragments) and had a depth bug making them elliptical tubes. Added jug/squat-jar/trigger-spray lathes. Shelf tags now one per SKU at that SKU's facing width (rail texture no longer prints fake tags). Discrete ceiling troffers with lens ribs and dark gaps. Darker shelf undersides + cavity gradient for bright/dark banding. Added 3 front-cross-aisle powerup spots at z=-16..-17 for the chase.

A corked 4m aisle is impassable: the thief's nav avoid radius (1.80m) is WIDER than the aisle half-lane (AISLE_GAP/2 - BODY_R = 1.58m), so he can never route around a cop standing in it and walks into the 1.15m catch radius. He needs counterplay — a back-of-store route, a second exit, or a juke past a blocking body. Then re-bench from enterFloor's actual spawn.

bench() measures a starting geometry the game never produces. bench() spawns the cop 4.32m BEHIND the thief (gapMul 0.96 x suspicionRadius, already at 0.7x copRun). game.js enterFloor(i) spawns him at (aisleX(i), 0, -AISLE_LEN/2+3) — the MOUTH of the thief's aisle, between the thief and the only exit. Measured from the real start with powerups deleted from the store: 100% catch, no powerup (80/80 controlled, 14/14 full end-to-end game loop), chase over in ~1.2s median. Root cause is geometry, not speed: a corked 4m aisle is impassable — the thief's own nav avoid radius (1.8m, agents.js navToExit bolt case) is WIDER than the aisle half-lane (AISLE_GAP/2 - BODY_R = 1.58m), so he can never route around a cop standing in it and walks straight into the 1.15m catchRadius. Give him a way through (second exit / back-of-store route / a juke or shove past a blocking body), THEN re-run bench() from enterFloor()'s spawn — that is the only number that describes the game.

Not a tuning problem — two real bugs. (1) Powerups sat mid-aisle with a 1.42m grab radius, so boostFrac was 0.45 in supposedly-unpowered chases; snapped to shelf lip with a lateral reach gate, now 0.02. (2) Nav routed off the config floor plan, not the store's actual colliders, so thieves ground along unmodelled furniture and escapes only ever came from the two clean aisles; new nav.js builds an occupancy grid from real colliders + Dijkstra field from the exit. (3) Thief had no stamina model.

Root cause was NOT tuning. Two real bugs. (1) Powerups sat on the aisle centreline with a 1.42m grab radius, so a pure-pursuit cop was boosted 45% of every 'no powerup' chase - that WAS the 58-71%. (2) Nav routed off config.js's floor plan, which knows nothing about the produce tables/dump bins/cart corral the store puts IN the lanes; thieves ground along geometry while the cop (who only steers at the thief) walked up - escapes only ever happened from aisles 0-1, the two clean ones. Replaced the ladder graph with grid nav off the real collider set (src/agents/nav.js: occupancy grid + Dijkstra exit field + clearance cost), gated pickups on lateral reach velocity, and gave the thief his own wind (fatigue + adrenaline) so both gas out together. MEASURED n=400 perfect-pursuit bot: no powerup 71% -> 1.5% caught, loses by 2.80m/9.2ft (was 8.78m/28.8ft), closest approach 2.23m; with a powerup reached, 76.9% (60.7% over all chases incl. ones where none was reachable); boost in hand 88.8%. Also fixed: standing still no longer earns harassment complaints.
Desk phase is near-unwinnable: ~12s from concealment tell to exit, 14 roster rows, only 3 of 7 subjects visible per camera.

Content gap, not a rendering gap. (1) Product facings are flat colour fields with grey bars instead of real printed type — ~60% of the tell. (2) ~8 box meshes recoloured, 5-8 identical copies per shelf; real shelves carry 6-15 SKUs of mixed height/width and something on nearly every shelf is a bottle/jar/pouch/bag. (3) Zero 'shopped' disorder — every face perfectly flush, unrotated, evenly spaced, no sold-out voids.

Added watchdogs so escaped/wedged thieves recycle and the store population stays at 14.
